Database Design · Group 8

Long-Life Shoe Factory

An integrated database design for production, orders, procurement, payments, and goods receipt.

Academic Case Study
CONTEXTFootwear Manufacturing
DELIVERABLESERD & Data Dictionary
TECHNICAL PRACTICESQL & MongoDB

Company Profile

The case study presents Long-Life Shoe Factory as an Indonesian footwear manufacturer established in 1990 and a leading participant in the national footwear industry. Its products emphasize quality, durability, and comfort for sports, work, and everyday use.

Business Needs

As the company expands, it requires more effective and efficient data management across increasingly complex operations:

  • Raw material and finished goods inventory.
  • Production scheduling and supervision.
  • Transaction, order, and delivery processing.
  • Payment monitoring and cash flow management.

Proposed Solution and Project Objectives

The project aims to design and build an integrated database system for the Long-Life case study. It applies database course concepts to practical operational data management, with the goal of improving efficiency, accuracy, productivity, and customer service.

The design brings five core business processes into a shared data model, supported by an entity relationship diagram and a data dictionary.

Five Core Business Processes

  1. Production

    Record production activities, quantities, dates, and status from planning to finished goods.

  2. Order Management

    Organize requests from internal teams and customers, including order status.

  3. Procurement

    Record purchases based on operational requirements and available budgets.

  4. Payment Management

    Track payment amounts, methods, and transaction status.

  5. Goods Receipt

    Document the receipt of goods by the company or the relevant recipient.

Explore the Database Design

Six Documented Data Entities

The report defines a product master and five operational entities. Its data dictionary specifies fields, data types, primary keys, and foreign keys.

  • Products
  • Production
  • Orders
  • Purchases
  • Payments
  • Goods Receipt

Query Practice

The coursework includes SQL exercises involving functions, joins, set operations, subqueries, and views, alongside MongoDB and Python examples for data retrieval and aggregation.

Intended Business Value

The proposed database provides a foundation for organized inventory records, production tracking, and transaction monitoring. These are intended benefits of the academic design; the report does not establish measured results from a production deployment.

Project Attribution
